evidence.claim: The data defect is real and exactly detectable. np.array_equal on consecutive uint16 volumes of three 6bba videos marks the same transitions as the '>80% zero-length predicted edges' proxy, plus one transition the proxy misses (about 1 in 10). The freeze pattern repeats across crops with a time offset: 05b6850b has freezes at [4,12,27,42,52,57,59,62,66,76] and 05db0fb1 has the same pattern shifted by +22. So freezes belong to the recording's acquisition clock, not to individual crops, and a hidden embryo either has them throughout or not at all.
evidence.source: local check, scratchpad rawdup.py on biohub-cell-tracking-during-development/train/*.zarr; notes file

evidence.claim: The GT does double its step after a freeze (hypothesis numbers reproduce exactly). GT step in um on frozen transitions: n=7991, median 0, p90 0, one outlier at 8.9 (the forum's 'GT moves up to 8.9 um'). Normal: n=94617, median 1.86, p90 4.16, 1.7% above 7 um. Post-freeze: n=6449, median 3.37, p90 7.80, 13.8% above 7 um.
evidence.source: local, train/*.geff (coordinates are voxels and need scaling) + edges_exp39.parquet frozen proxy

evidence.claim: Velocity persistence in GT tracks shows the post-freeze step is two frames of motion. Regressing step t on step t-1 gives beta 0.37 on normal steps. After a k=1 freeze it gives 0.80, i.e. about 0.4 x (k+1). The best prediction weight for k=1 is 0.8-1.0 x v_pre: median residual drops from 3.30 to 2.93 um and the share above 5.5 um from 21.9% to 13.5%. Extrapolating with the full (k+1)*v = 2v is WORSE than no prediction (median 3.83, 25.8% above 5.5 um). For k=2 (n=113) beta is 0.32 and there is no gain. For k=3 (n=165) beta is 1.41.

In code, motion_relink_edges sets predecessor_position_um[target] = pos[source]. After a freeze the source's predecessor is its own frozen twin, so v is about 0. The tight 5.5 and relaxed 10 um gates test the RAW distance |target - source|, not the motion residual. Post-freeze raw p90 is 7.47 against 4.14 normally, a factor of 1.8.

The proposed motion-model change is worth nothing once the edge filter runs. I re-ran the relink Hungarian on post-freeze frames only (raw t55 nodes, learned probabilities, predecessors from the exp39 relink cache; the baseline reproduces 98.6% of cached relink edges; per-frame 7 um Hungarian GT matching; frame-local copy of the edge filter with alt=3, relink=1, max_prob 0.3). SELECTION, 6bba post frames, TP/FP/FN: base+ef 2949/336/384; velocity carry w=0.5*(k+1) 2950/336/383; tight gate scaled by sqrt(k+1) 2947/334/386. Before the edge filter, velocity carry gave +9 TP / -8 FP, and scaling both gates by sqrt(k+1) gave +31 TP / +58 FP, a net LOSS at J~0.9.

What does help: on post-freeze transitions, keep the ILP's own edges first and let the relink fill only the nodes the ILP left unmatched. With the edge filter applied, on post frames: SELECTION ILP-only 2988/302/345 (+39 TP, -34 FP vs base+ef), ILP+fill 3022/349/311 (+73 TP, +13 FP). CONFIRMATION 6bba: base+ef 2840/210/276, ILP-only 2913/178/203 (+73 TP, -32 FP), ILP+fill 2927/228/189 (+87 TP, +18 FP). Both halves are positive.

The ILP advantage is specific to post-freeze frames. On a control sample of normal frames (every 7th, selection, with the edge filter), ILP+fill gives +15 TP / +5 FP per 6922 GT edges (0.2%), against +73/+13 per 3333 (2.2%) on post frames, about 10x larger relative. Before the edge filter the gap is +0.8% vs +5.7%. Global relink-off lost 0.002 on the LB, so the network's local advantage is optimistic. Here that optimism is diluted by a real handicap of the relink (v=0, one-step gate).
evidence.source: local, scratchpad sim3.py / sim5.py; CONTEXT.md (relink-off LB -0.002)

evidence.claim: Classical trackers scale the Brownian search radius with sqrt(time gap) (u-track brownScaling 0.5 up to timeReachConfB, then linScaling 0.01). That supports the sqrt(k+1) form of any gate, but our simulation shows gate widening adds more FP than TP in this dense field.

No public Kaggle notebook or repo handles post-freeze transitions specially. The forum only lists frozen frames per video (Tom, discussion 724283) and says GT jumps after duplicated or dropped frames (729053 etc.).

implementation_notes: (1) Detection in the kernel: frozen_t = {t : np.array_equal(vol[t], vol[t+1])} on the raw uint16 zarr, 99 comparisons per video, a few seconds. Do NOT use the 'identical detections' proxy: the temporal UNet sees neighbouring frames, so twins give non-identical detections (only 234 of 909 frozen transitions have >95% zero-length edges), and the >80% zero proxy misses about 1 in 10 raw freezes. Post-freeze transition = t with t-1 in frozen_t and t not in frozen_t; k = length of the freeze run ending at t-1. 44b6 has no freezes, so the rule is an exact no-op there. (2) The change that carries the gain: in motion_relink_edges, for t in post_set, seed frame_matches with the ILP solution edges s->d (t->t+1, one-to-one; the same dict edgefilter_final_graph receives as ilp_probs), remove their endpoints from unmatched_sources/targets, then run the usual tight/relaxed passes on the leftovers (variant FILL) or skip them (variant ILPONLY). Set predecessor_position_um for the seeded edges as usual, and give them edge_prob = ILP p so the edge filter never touches them. (3) Velocity carry is harmless but worth ~0 after the edge filter. If kept: store vel[target] = vel[source] when the transition is frozen, else pos[target] - pos[source]; predict src + 0.5*(k+1)*vel. Never use (k+1)*v at full weight: the GT-optimal weight is about 0.4*(k+1) and 2v is worse than 0. (4) Do NOT scale the relink gates: sqrt(k+1) on both gates was net negative before the edge filter and neutral after it. GAP_CLOSE_UM already scales with gap+1. (5) Linefit real time (map each duplicate onto its twin's time) is GT-correct: GT on frozen pairs has median 0, while linefit currently spreads twins to about 0.97 um. Its score effect is unmeasured and probably tiny under 7 um matching (my guess). (6) Unverified claim from the hypothesis: 13 of 125 GT divisions fall on post-freeze transitions. Safe-division gate scaling is untested and low value (23 division TP in total). (7) Pitfalls: my simulation evaluates per frame with a per-frame Hungarian GT match, not the official timepoint-aware matcher, and ignores knock-on effects on the next transition's predecessor velocities, gap closing, stitch and short-track filtering. The ILP numbers are locally optimistic because the edge net was trained on all 199 train videos. Watch the node multiplier: FILL adds edges, not nodes, so N_pred is unchanged.
refined_change: Replace the motion-model idea with 'ILP-first on post-freeze transitions'. In the kernel, detect exact duplicate raw volumes (np.array_equal). For every transition that directly follows a freeze run, accept the ILP solution's t->t+1 edges as they are, and let the motion relink assign only the nodes the ILP left unmatched (FILL). The alternative is ILP-only, with no relink on that transition. Everything downstream (gap closing, gap2, safe divisions, short-track filter, linefit, edge filter, stitch, DaughterNet) runs unchanged. Optional and near-free: carry the pre-freeze velocity with weight 0.5*(k+1). Drop the gate scaling. Linefit real time is optional and probably below noise.
refined_lab_test: Replay-lab patch 'postfreeze' on top of the current best tail (exp39 + edge filter alt3/relink, plus stitch if that is the base being probed). Knob POSTFREEZE_MODE in {0 = off (control, must be bit-identical to the base), 1 = ILPONLY, 2 = FILL}. Frozen set from np.array_equal of raw frames; the replay needs the raw zarr, or a precomputed per-stem frozen list (cheap, CPU). (a) SELECTION (64 6bba): run modes 1 and 2 and pick one. Read out TP/FP/FN by transition class (normal / frozen / post / post+1) with parquet columns t and len_pre_um, or better the exact raw-equality list. (b) One CONFIRMATION run (135 videos) with the chosen mode. Success: 44b6 bit-identical (71/71 unchanged); 6bba confirmation delta >= +0.0008 with 90% CI lower bound > 0; gains on >= 55% of CHANGED 6bba videos; normal-transition TP/FP within +-0.0002 score (only post+1 predecessor effects may move them). The protocol criterion 'each embryo >= +0.001' must become '44b6 identical', otherwise the gate rejects any 6bba-only rule by construction. My offline expectation (per-frame approximation): ILPONLY about +112 TP / -66 FP and FILL about +160 TP / +31 FP pooled over all 128 6bba videos. Runs on Kaggle CPU kernels only; no GPU needed.
expected_gain: The proposed motion-model change (velocity x(k+1) plus gate scaling): about 0.0000 after the edge filter (measured offline); drop it. The refined 'ILP-first on post-freeze transitions': about +0.0010 to +0.0013 local on 6bba (hypothesis scale of 7.4e-6 per edge; per-frame approximation, locally optimistic because the edge net saw these videos), 0 on 44b6. Expected public LB: +0.0000 to +0.0008. This is a guess: the local gain is halved for network optimism and multiplied by P(hidden embryo has duplicate frames), which I put at ~0.5. Freezes are a property of the recording, so a hidden embryo either has them throughout or not at all. There is no downside if the hidden embryos have no freezes. This is a small, safe add-on, not a path to 0.97.
